static_traits.name: Chen Anming
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior psychological counseling or treatment; no similar psychological problems before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, can give concrete examples; emotionally mainly frustration and self-blame; skeptical about cognitive reappraisal but willing to try; cooperation acceptable.

basic_info.main_problem: I tend to label myself negatively based on small mistakes, leading to a sense of incompetence and self-criticism. These feelings began a few months ago when I scratched the board while unloading my water skis from the truck; the problem then developed into often labeling myself 'stupid' for small errors, especially in activities I enjoy (like water skiing).
basic_info.core_demands: I just want to stop feeling so bad about myself all the time. I want to enjoy the things I love again without constantly reproaching myself for every small mistake.
growth_experiences: A few months ago, Chen Anming accidentally scratched his water skis while unloading them from the truck. At the time he blamed his own carelessness, with moderate initial stress. The problem then gradually worsened, developing into labeling himself 'stupid' whenever he made small mistakes, especially in water-skiing-related situations. He tried reminding himself that 'mistakes happen' and focusing on the positive, but could not shake the self-criticism; the incident has had a lasting impact on his self-esteem and enjoyment of activities.

special_situations.event: A few months ago, scratched the water ski while unloading it from the truck
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make mistakes on seemingly simple things, it means I am stupid and my abilities are inadequate
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly blaming myself afterwards to prevent repeat mistakes, while trying to remind myself that 'mistakes happen, focus on the positive', but it hardly works
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am so stupid; how can I not even do this little thing well

special_situations.event: Last weekend, tried to fix a loose pin on a ski binding but made the problem worse
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot do something well in one try, it proves my overall ability is low
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sets a high standard of 'must do it right' for oneself, uses harsh criticism to urge oneself to avoid mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am really too stupid; I cannot even fix this

special_situations.event: Once a small error occurs in an activity she loves (such as water skiing)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make small mistakes in activities I value, it means I am incompetent and not worthy of enjoying them
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly ruminating and self-criticizing, trying to counter with 'reality testing/positive reminders', but cannot keep it up
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This shows I am not capable/I cannot do anything well

special_situations.event: Immediately self-evaluates after any small error appears
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Mistakes represent low overall ability; positive evidence is not important
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses on error details while ignoring existing abilities and past successes, uses harsh criticism to maintain high standards
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This proves again that I am not good enough

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen as capable, maintain self-esteem, and enjoy interest activities freely
core_conflict.fear: Fearing that once I make a mistake I will be labeled 'stupid/incompetent', thereby negating my self-worth
defense_goal: Controlling Anxiety and avoiding mistakes by setting excessively high standards and self-criticizing
Maintains tight control over performance to protect fragile self-esteem

object_relations.self_representation: Experiences oneself as a failure who is prone to mistakes and clumsy
object_relations.object_representation: The inner other is represented as a harsh judge (mistakes are negated)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes conducting 'reality testing / cognitive reappraisal' or encourages viewing mistakes from a more lenient perspective
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing these methods may be ineffective for oneself ('I am not sure looking at it this way will change anything')
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Restrained tone, expressing doubt in declarative statements, reducing emotional wording, emphasizing 'may be ineffective/uncertain', giving limited agreement to the counselor's suggestions while keeping distance.

manifestations: Having several friends to talk with, but not yet sharing these negative self-labels and thoughts with them
Tending to bear it alone when making mistakes and blaming oneself, not seeking others' understanding and support
outcomes: Decreased self-esteem, reduced enjoyment of activities
Self-criticism intensifies; negative experiences are amplified

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Expressing in conversation the belief 'I should always do everything right'
Setting rigid perfection standards for oneself, equating mistakes with being unworthy or incompetent

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: After making a mistake, quickly makes the worst self-assessment and repeatedly self-blames
Repeatedly expressing the limiting statement 'I am not sure this will change anything' during sessions

positive_force: Willing to try new perspectives and methods (though doubtful, willing to explore)
Able to identify and describe specific negative thought patterns and trigger situations
Investment in interests like water skiing is a potential positive resource
Has a certain degree of social support (friends to talk with)
Able to consider the perspective that others would be more tolerant of mistakes, showing some cognitive flexibility
negative_force: Rigid 'should'-style high standards and perfectionist tendencies
Cognitive patterns of overgeneralization, personalization and negating the positive
Self-deprecating labels (equating a single error with overall ability)
Not seeking support during negative experiences, leading to worsened isolation and rumination

target_behavior.behavior: Immediately after making a mistake, labels herself 'stupid' and repeatedly blames herself
antecedent: Sees or makes small mistakes (such as scratching the skis when removing them)
When an error occurs in a liked activity (such as failing to repair a ski part)
The moment of self-assessment when noticing any tiny mistake
target_behavior.core_reason: Holding black-and-white standards toward mistakes and overgeneralized beliefs (treating one mistake as overall incompetence), and tending to personalize occasional events as character flaws
target_behavior.function: Tries through self-reproach to control and reduce mistakes, maintaining a sense of control over performance
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired self-esteem, Activity enjoyment declining, Negative emotions worsening, more avoidance and rumination emerging
